extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers of scientific method, natural philosophy, and history/philosophy of science
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and procedural criteria for discovering 'forms' or natures by Baconian induction: constructing exclusion tables, using comparative (comparential) tables, permitting provisional hypotheses, selecting ostensive instances, and formulating true differentiae (illustrated with the enquiry into the 'form of heat').

rubrics_metrics.name: Double Method of Agreement / Joint Method (agreement + difference)
rubrics_metrics.description: If both conditions (agreement and difference) are satisfied, the case falls under the Double Method of Agreement (or Joint Method of Agreement and Difference) and it would be proved that the ascertained cause was not only a cause but the only cause of the given phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both the method of agreement (common concomitants) and the method of difference (presence/absence contrasts) together to exclude plurality of causes; only when both are satisfied can one claim the cause is the sole one. See related notes on plurality of causes and Aph. 4 and Aph. 13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of Exclusions / Rejection (Exclusiva)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection or exclusiva of simple natures consists in showing a candidate nature is not the form by finding it absent where the given nature is present, present where the given nature is absent, or varying inversely with the given nature (increase vs decrease).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct tables of instances exhibiting: (a) the candidate nature not in any instance where the given nature is present; (b) the candidate nature present where the given nature is absent; (c) the candidate nature increasing when the given nature decreases; (d) decreasing when the given nature increases. Use multiple instances and repeat where clarity requires; exhaustive rejection strengthens the induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustive exclusion as prerequisite to affirmative form
rubrics_metrics.description: After rejection and due exhaustive exclusion, what remains (as if in the background) will be the affirmative form: 'forma affirmativa, solida, et vera'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exclusiva lays the foundations of true induction but is not complete until the affirmative interpretation (sistatur in affirmativa) is established. Rejection must be so exhaustive that only one candidate cause remains—conditions rarely perfectly met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against imposing customary or familiar forms (cognitive bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware that because many attributes appear to pertain to forms, they may be dragged to forms to which human contemplation is accustomed; avoid allowing familiar concepts to determine forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let received opinions, scholastic abstractions, or customary classifications shape your assignment of forms. Seek evidence-driven determination rather than conformity with habitual conceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceive 'forms' as laws/determinations of pure act tied to operative reality
rubrics_metrics.description: When speaking of forms, understand them as the laws and determinations of pure act which ordain and constitute a simple nature (e.g., forma caloris = lex caloris), not as purely abstract Plato-like forms divorced from material operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep forms connected to the operative parts and observable effects (calor, lumen, pondus, etc.). Avoid purely abstract, non-determinate definitions; treat forms as laws governing behavior of matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the three tables of Comparentia and the Vindemiatio Prima (permissio intellectus)
rubrics_metrics.description: After preparing initial comparential tables and exclusions, permit the intellect to begin an affirmative interpretation ('permissio intellectus' or 'vindemiationem primam') using the tables of comparentia as the basis for a tentative reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vindemiatio prima rests directly on the three tables of Comparentia (Tab. 3 etc.) and is a provisional interpretive step that helps extract emergent truths from error; it should not replace or contradict thorough Exclusiva but may guide further inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer ostensive instances (instantias ostensive) where form is most conspicuous
rubrics_metrics.description: Select instances in which the form is more conspicuous and less impeded by other natures—these 'instantias ostensive' show the form more evidently and are used to advance the vindemiatio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify cases where the nature is least cohibited and least mixed with other influences; such instances better display the candidate form and are primary evidence for tentative affirmative claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for Plurality of Causes before rejecting a candidate cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Objection from the Plurality of Causes: the given nature might be produced by other causes, so a mere concomitance does not suffice to warrant rejection unless all possible causes have been considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that exclusions consider alternative causal agents; a rejection is only justified when the exclusion is exhaustive with respect to all plausible causes. Recognize that demonstrating co-occurrence does not prove uniqueness of cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow provisional hypotheses (Permissio Intellectus) as heuristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Bacon seems to condemn hypothesis elsewhere, he allows 'permissio intellectus'—the mind may be permitted to follow a natural course and use hypotheses provisionally to point the way to truer theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hypotheses and tentative interpretations to guide experiments and further inductive work, recognizing they are aids and must be tested and ultimately grounded by Exclusiva and affirmative induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct exemplifying exclusion tables (illustrated by the exclusions for the form of heat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete exclusion examples to eliminate candidate natures for a form—e.g., the text lists many exclusions for 'forma calidi' (reject terrestrial nature by solar rays; reject celestial nature by common fire; reject subtilior texture by heating many classes of bodies; reject light/lumen distinctions by specific experiments; reject tenuity by behavior of heated metals/air; reject uniform local expansion etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate exclusion tables with diverse, cross-class instances (minerals, vegetables, animals, liquids, gases, metals, celestial rays) that show presence/absence or inverse variation patterns. The long enumerated exclusions for heat serve as a model of exhaustive, varied negative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize Exclusiva as the foundation but incomplete without affirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundations of true induction are laid in the Exclusiva (rejections), yet the Exclusiva by itself is not perfect and cannot be the final conclusion—affirmative synthesis is required for completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat rejections as necessary groundwork. Do not present Exclusiva results as final until they are integrated into an affirmative, well-confirmed formulation of the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectify vague notions of simple natures; avoid acquiescence to ill-defined concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Notions such as 'elementaris', 'coelestis', 'tenuitatis' are often vague and ill-termined; investigators must not rest in such notions but must further prosecute inquiry and strengthen concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use induction to clarify and define simple natures; do not accept coarse or traditional labels without refining their definitions through systematic empirical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require the form to be present in all instances of the thing (universality test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A form of a thing must be present in all and every instance in which the thing itself is present; otherwise it would not be the form. Hence no true contradictory instance should exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for universal concomitants across all instances; if a purported form fails to be present in some instances, it cannot be the true form. Use universality as a criterion to validate candidate forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish the quality itself from sensory affection and from means of production
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish 'calor' (heat itself) from 'calidum' (the sensible effect on organisms) and from 'calefactivum' (the agent or means that produces heating); do not conflate propagation/communication of heat with the form of heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in terminology and causal accounts: separate the intrinsic nature (form), its sensory perceptions, and the mechanisms by which it is produced or communicated. Test candidate distinctions experimentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulate true differentiae to limit and constitute the species (illustration: three differentiae of heat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the differentiae that limit the genus and constitute the species. For heat Bacon proposes (1) 'calor sit motus expansivus' (heat is expansive motion), (2) 'calor sit motus expansivus sive versus circumferentiam' with an upward tendency, and (3) 'calor sit motus, non expansivus uniformiter secundum totum, sed expansivus per particulas minores corporis' (expansion by smaller particles, not uniformly of the whole).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive specific, testable discriminating properties (differentiae) from evidence; beware equivocal or delusive differentiations and refine through experiment and comparative instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design controlled experiments to test predicted properties (experimental checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use designed experiments (e.g., heating rods with snow placed above vs below to test directionality of heat/frigus; comparing perpendicularly vs laterally immersed iron in flame) to test whether predicted motions or effects actually occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate candidate differentiae and exclusions into concrete experimental setups that isolate variables and observe predicted contrasts; use such experiments to confirm or refute tentative vindemiatio claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious of delusive or spurious differentiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some differentiations (for example, the second differentiation about upward tendency) may be delusive and require careful examination: 'It will be seen ... that this second differentiation is delusive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept differentiations at face value; check them against a wide range of instances and experiments. Mark and discard delusive generalizations uncovered by further induction.
